newsitem.title: UK: Insurance buyers ready to use internet,study shows.
newsitem.headline: Insurance buyers ready to use internet,study shows.

text.p: British consumers are increasingly prepared to buy insurance over the internet, but are not yet ready to buy it from companies based in other European countries, according to a survey to be published on Wednesday.

Insurers have speculated for some time on the potential for media such as the internet to become significant sales vehicles, and the new survey by Swiss Re and the Henley research centre indicates that the wealthier and younger sections of the public agree.
In a poll of 1,513 adults, 22 per cent were positive about the concept using computers to buy personal insurance, such as for cars, travel ,and home contents.
The figure rose to 29 percent among 25-34 year-olds.
But the greatest interest was in using the internet to shop around and make price comparisons, with 67 per cent of respondents choosing this facility as the main use for on-screen services.

"This begins to suggest how the telephone potentially may be used in tandem with the screen; the latter providing the search, select, and quote facility, while the 'phone remains the sales execution tool," the report said.

But while Britons are overcoming their fears of technology and of committing financial details to the internet, they are becoming tougher on their reluctance to buy from insurers based elsewhere in Europe.

Around 58 per cent said they would definitely not buy from a company elsewhere in Europe, while another 17 per cent said it was fairly unlikely. This compared with 55 per cent and 19 percent in a similar survey in 1995.

"Although the attractiveness of continental European providers has decreased relative to 1995, there are still significant minorities of consumers (19 per cent) and small businesses (34 per cent), who would consider cross border purchases of insurance," the report said.
Again 18-24 year-olds and those in AB socio-economic groups were most open to the idea.
However it concluded: "For continental insurers, it seems that for the time being it is still a case of 'think global, act local!'"
